Algorithm: CountSort(A, n, exp)

1. For i <- 0 to 9 do
2.        bucket[i] <- 0
3. For i <- 0 to (n-1) do
4.        d <- (A[i]/exp) mod 10
5.        bucket[d] <- bucket[d]+1
6. For i <- 1 to 9 do
7.        bucket[i] <- bucket[i]+bucket[i-1]
8. For i <- (n-1) down to 0 do
9.        d <- (A[i]/exp) mod 10
10.       bucket[d] <- bucket[d]-1
11.       output[bucket[d]] <- A[i]
12. For i <- 0 to (n-1) do
13.       A[i] <- output[i]
14. Return

aim: Write a program in c to sort the elements using quick sort and find its execution time using the time function.
algorithm:
Algorithm: QuickSort(A, low, high)

1. Start
2. If (low < high) then
3.        p <- Partition(A, low, high)
4.        QuickSort(A, low, p-1)
5.        QuickSort(A, p+1, high)
6. Stop

Algorithm: Partition(A, low, high)

1. pivot <- A[high]
2. i <- low-1
3. For j <- low to (high-1) do
4.        if A[j] <= pivot then
5.              i <- i+1
6.              swap A[i] and A[j]
7. swap A[i+1] and A[high]
8. Return i+1

6.        Merge(A, low, mid, high)

Algorithm: Merge(A, low, mid, high)

1. n1 <- mid-low+1, n2 <- high-mid
2. Copy A[low..mid] into L[0..n1-1] and A[mid+1..high] into R[0..n2-1]
3. i <- 0, j <- 0, k <- low
4. While (i < n1 and j < n2) do
5.        if L[i] <= R[j] then
6.              A[k] <- L[i], i <- i+1
7.        else
8.              A[k] <- R[j], j <- j+1
9.        k <- k+1
10. Copy the remaining elements of L and R into A
11. Return

aim: Write a program in c to find the longest common subsequence (LCS) of two sequences using dynamic programming and find its execution time using the time function.
algorithm:
Algorithm: LCS-Length(X, Y, m, n)

1. Start

3.        c[i][0] <- 0
4. For j <- 0 to n do
5.        c[0][j] <- 0
6. For i <- 1 to m do

8.              if X[i] == Y[j] then
9.                    c[i][j] <- c[i-1][j-1] + 1
10.                   b[i][j] <- 'D'
11.             else if c[i-1][j] >= c[i][j-1] then
12.                   c[i][j] <- c[i-1][j]
13.                   b[i][j] <- 'U'
14.             else
15.                   c[i][j] <- c[i][j-1]
16.                   b[i][j] <- 'L'
17. print "Length of LCS" c[m][n]
18. PrintLCS(b, X, m, n)
19. Stop

Algorithm: PrintLCS(b, X, i, j)

1. If (i == 0 or j == 0) then
2.        Return
3. If b[i][j] == 'D' then
4.        PrintLCS(b, X, i-1, j-1)
5.        print X[i]
6. else if b[i][j] == 'U' then
7.        PrintLCS(b, X, i-1, j)
8. else
9.        PrintLCS(b, X, i, j-1)

aim: Write a program in c to solve the fractional knapsack problem using the greedy method and find its execution time using the time function.
algorithm:
Algorithm: FractionalKnapsack(v, w, n, W)

1. Start
2. For i <- 1 to n do
3.        r[i] <- v[i]/w[i]
4.        x[i] <- 0
5. Sort the items in decreasing order of r[i] (merge sort)
6. remaining <- W, total <- 0
7. For each item i in sorted order, while remaining > 0 do
8.        if w[i] <= remaining then
9.              x[i] <- 1
10.             remaining <- remaining - w[i]
11.       else
12.             x[i] <- remaining/w[i]
13.             remaining <- 0
14.       total <- total + x[i]*v[i]
15. print "Maximum value" total
16. Stop

aim: Write a program in c to solve the travelling salesman problem using dynamic programming and find its execution time using the time function.
algorithm:
Algorithm: TSP(cost, n)
(g(i, S) = cheapest path that starts at city i, visits every city in set S once, and ends at city 1)

1. Start
2. For i <- 2 to n do
3.        g(i, {}) <- cost[i][1]
4. For each set S not containing city 1, in increasing size do
5.        For each city i not in S do
6.              g(i, S) <- infinity
7.              For each city k in S do
8.                    if cost[i][k] + g(k, S - {k}) < g(i, S) then
9.                          g(i, S) <- cost[i][k] + g(k, S - {k})
10.                         next(i, S) <- k
11. print "Minimum cost" g(1, {2, 3, ..., n})
12. Follow next(i, S) from city 1 to print the tour
13. Stop

aim: Write a program in c to solve the job assignment problem using branch and bound and find its execution time using the time function.
algorithm:
Algorithm: JOB-ASSIGNMENT(C, n)   (Least Cost Branch and Bound)
(lb(X) = cost of the jobs assigned so far in X
         + for every worker not yet assigned, his cheapest job among the jobs still free)

1. Start
2. Create the root node: no worker assigned, cost <- 0
3. lb(root) <- lower bound of root
4. Insert root into the list of live nodes
5. While the list of live nodes is not empty do
6.       E <- the live node with minimum lb
7.       Remove E from the list of live nodes
8.       if all n workers are assigned in E then
9.             print the assignment in E and its cost as the optimal solution
10.            Stop
11.      i <- the next worker to be assigned in E
12.      For each job j not yet assigned in E do
13.            Create a child X of E with worker i assigned job j
14.            cost(X) <- cost(E) + C[i][j]
15.            lb(X) <- lower bound of X
16.            Insert X into the list of live nodes
17. Stop

aim: Write a program in c to find the shortest path from a source vertex to all other vertices using Dijkstra's algorithm and find its execution time using the time function.
algorithm:
Algorithm: DA(G, w, s)

1. INITIALIZE-SINGLE-SOURCE(G, s)
2. S <- Ø
3. Q <- V[G]
4. while Q != Ø
5.       do u <- EXTRACT-MIN(Q)
6.          S <- S U {u}
7.          for each vertex v in Adj[u]
8.                do RELAX(u, v, w)

INITIALIZE-SINGLE-SOURCE(G, s)
1. for each vertex v in V[G]
2.       do d[v] <- infinity
3.          p[v] <- NIL
4. d[s] <- 0

EXTRACT-MIN(Q)
1. u <- the vertex in Q with minimum d[u]
2. Q <- Q - {u}
3. return u

RELAX(u, v, w)
1. if d[v] > d[u] + w(u,v)
2.       then d[v] <- d[u] + w(u,v)
3.            p[v] <- u

aim: Write a program in c to find the shortest paths between all pairs of vertices using the Floyd-Warshall algorithm and find its execution time using the time function.
algorithm:
Algorithm: FLOYD-WARSHALL(W)

1. Start
2. n <- number of vertices
3. For i <- 1 to n do
4.        For j <- 1 to n do
5.              if i == j then D[i][j] <- 0
6.              else if there is an edge (i,j) then D[i][j] <- W[i][j]
7.              else D[i][j] <- infinity
8. For k <- 1 to n do
9.        For i <- 1 to n do
10.             For j <- 1 to n do
11.                   if D[i][k] + D[k][j] < D[i][j] then
12.                         D[i][j] <- D[i][k] + D[k][j]
13. Print D
14. Stop

aim: Write a program in c to find the minimum cost spanning tree of a graph using Prim's algorithm and find its execution time using the time function.
algorithm:
Algorithm: MST-PRIM(G, w, r)

1. for each u in V[G]
2.       do key[u] <- infinity
3.          p[u] <- NIL
4. key[r] <- 0
5. Q <- V[G]
6. while Q != Ø
7.       do u <- EXTRACT-MIN(Q)
8.          for each v in Adj[u]
9.                do if v in Q and w(u,v) < key[v]
10.                     then p[v] <- u
11.                          key[v] <- w(u,v)

EXTRACT-MIN(Q)
1. u <- the vertex in Q with minimum key[u]
2. Q <- Q - {u}
3. return u

aim: Write a program in c to find the minimum cost spanning tree of a graph using Kruskal's algorithm and find its execution time using the time function.
algorithm:
Algorithm: MST-KRUSKAL(G, w)

1. A <- Ø
2. for each vertex v in V[G]
3.       do MAKE-SET(v)
4. sort the edges of E into nondecreasing order by weight w
5. for each edge (u,v) in E, taken in nondecreasing order by weight
6.       do if FIND-SET(u) != FIND-SET(v)
7.             then A <- A U {(u,v)}
8.                  UNION(u,v)
9. return A

MAKE-SET(x)
1. parent[x] <- x
2. rank[x] <- 0

FIND-SET(x)
1. if x != parent[x]
2.       then parent[x] <- FIND-SET(parent[x])
3. return parent[x]

UNION(x, y)
1. x <- FIND-SET(x), y <- FIND-SET(y)
2. if rank[x] > rank[y]
3.       then parent[y] <- x
4.       else parent[x] <- y
5.            if rank[x] == rank[y]
6.                  then rank[y] <- rank[y] + 1
